description: The builder binds a review only by checking that the substring "](" + review_path + ")" occurs somewhere in the claim's own PROOF_INDEX bullet. Every reviewed bullet also links the claim's proof. The D2 bullet also links bare main#67, which the bullet says 'remains open for other bundled fronts'. So a CLAIM_SPECS entry whose review is the proof path (or #67) passes project(). museum_check.py regenerates exactly those bytes. The frontend guard accepts them too: for a non-pointer review it only requires sourceContainsPath(quote, review). Nothing checks that the review differs from the proof or fills the review role in the bullet. The frontend check is looser still. Any link in the quote passes, and so does any path that is a suffix of a link, including a mutable branch URL. The D5 AMEND row links .../Math-/blob/main/PROOF_INDEX.md, so the pinned index itself passes as the D5 card's 'Byte-verified review'. Dropping pointer_only also skips the D5_OPEN_REVIEW binding, and the card then shows 'Byte-verified review' next to 'Unmerged review pointer only'. The P15 counterexample card accepts LANDING_CLAIMS.json the same way. The only negative control (test_misdirected_review_pointer_refused) uses a path that is absent from the bullet, so it cannot detect this. The shipped cd32303 museum.json is correct (p0 baseline). The defect is that no layer refuses the substitution.
why: On an ACCEPT-scoped card, the author's own candidate body, or the landing inventory, can appear as the 'Byte-verified review'. That is a review the source does not support. The path is one wrong CLAIM_SPECS entry, a hand-edited table, and builder, CI check and browser guard all pass it. This is exactly the proof/review substitution the museum claims to prevent, and the existing control gives false assurance.

verdicts.reasoning:
I reproduced the core defect at the cd32303 bytes with my own probes in probes/verify_substitution_1/. I used no network: urlopen and fetch are stubbed. Every fixture source is re-verified against the builder's own SOURCES pins (29 of 30; only README.md@d6628da is missing offline). The cd32303 tree was not modified (0 files newer than the probes).

Code facts at cd32303:
- tools/museum_data.py:403-406 binds a reviewed claim's review only by checking that "](" + review_path + ")" appears somewhere in that claim's own bullet. Every bullet also links the claim's proof, so review := proof passes.
- The builder never binds the review targets of the open rows (open_specs, about lines 421-433) to their STATUS rows.
- tools/museum_check.py:37-43 only regenerates build() and compares bytes (check_export), then runs test_museum_frontend.mjs. It has no review-role logic of its own.
- docs/site/museum.mjs:86 (non-pointer branch) requires only sourceContainsPath(quote, review). Lines 51-53 accept any link in the quote, or any `/${path})` suffix. The D5 AMEND row links the mutable .../Math-/blob/main/PROOF_INDEX.md, so the pinned index descriptor passes as that row's non-pointer review. Dropping pointer_only skips line 85 and its D5_OPEN_REVIEW binding. renderClaim (151, 153) then prints "Byte-verified review" next to "Unmerged review pointer only".
- No frontend test exercises the "Review file differs" branch at all.

Corrections to the finding:
1. Its headline builder examples B (D2 review := its proof) and C (D2 review := bare main#67) are NOT accepted by every layer. Both are caught by an existing CI unit test the finding misses: tests/test_museum_data.py:95-103, test_review_pointers_do_not_claim_comment_byte_custody, run by public-shop.yml:25. That test pins claims[0..2] to pointer_only + PROOF_INDEX.md + '#issuecomment-', and claims[3] to the pr28 path. So the claims "the only negative control is test_misdirected_review_pointer_refused" and "no layer refuses" are wrong for claims 0-3.
2. They hold for claims 4-10 and for the open rows. Self-substitution is accepted by the builder and passes the CI unit suite for:
   - d5-height-window
   - d5-two-scale
   - d5-inner-belt
   - cumulative-transfer
   - d6-p15-full-price
   - p15 := claims/LANDING_CLAIMS.json
3. The frontend then renders the d5-two-scale card with "Open review" == the proof's html_url under "Byte-verified review".
4. The D5-pin case does not need a hand-edited museum.json. A one-entry change in the builder's open_specs (review_target "PROOF_INDEX.md") is accepted by project(), passes the unit suite, and passes validateBoundManifest through the suffix clause.
5. The same logic is still present on current main 513261bb (museum_data.py:431-432; museum.mjs:66-68 and 105).

Scope: museum_data.py and museum.mjs are in the offered scope. Proof-as-review substitution is the proof/review substitution the offer names. For D2, the bare main#67 is also literally the P15 card's review pointer, a cross-claim case, though the unit test catches it.

Severity: I agree with critical, because the rubric's first branch is met literally. With every builder, CI and browser guard green, a card can label the author's own candidate body, or the pinned index on an AMEND/open card, as a "Byte-verified review" the source does not support. The guard was written precisely to refuse a misdirected review (test_misdirected_review_pointer_refused).

Mitigating facts that keep this from being a live misstatement:
- The shipped museum.json is correct (baseline equality confirmed).
- The path requires an author edit to a hard-coded spec, not external input.
- The verbatim scope quote on the same card still names the real review.
- class and source_label (the status labels) are separately guarded and unaffected.

The finding text should drop B and C as evidence (or note they are caught), and cite A, the other self-substitutions of claims 4-10, P15 and the open_specs D5-pin path instead.

description: PROOF_INDEX links reviews by relative path, which means 'this path at the index's own commit d6628da'. The frontend binds the proof to index_source.repository and commit, but for a non-pointer review it checks only that the path appears in the quote. A review descriptor for the same path at any other Math- commit, or in the query- repository, passes. The card then renders 'Byte-verified review' with that other identity. In the probe the alternate bytes are a synthetic stand-in for 'the same file at another commit', with the R7 verdict flipped to AMEND. They are verified against their own digest and shown under the ACCEPT-scoped card. The builder has the same gap: project() never compares SOURCES[review].commit or repository with INDEX. why: 'Byte-verified' then only proves that the bytes match their own digest. It does not prove they are the review the pinned index cites. A pre-review draft, an amended version, or a same-named file in another repository can be shown as the claim's review. The proof side shows this binding was intended.

verdicts.reasoning:
I checked the bytes first. The extracted docs/site/museum.mjs, docs/site/museum.json, tools/museum_data.py, tools/museum_check.py and docs/site/core.mjs have the same sha256 as `git show cd32303:<path>`. The harness imports museum.mjs and museum_data.py from that extracted tree, and global fetch and urlopen are stubbed so the probes make no network calls.

**The defect is real at cd32303.**
- museum.mjs:75 binds a reviewed claim's proof to index_source.repository and index_source.commit.
- museum.mjs:86 checks a non-pointer review only with sourceContainsPath(quote, review). That check is a path or suffix match on the quote, so the review's repository and commit are never compared with the index.
- The builder has the same gap. museum_data.py:405-406 calls descriptor(review_path), which takes whatever SOURCES[path] pins, and project() never compares that pin with INDEX.
- The PROOF_INDEX bullets cite every one of these reviews by a relative link "](reviews/...)", which means "this path at the index's commit d6628da".
- tests/test_museum_data.py and tests/test_museum_frontend.mjs have no negative control for a review pinned at the wrong commit.
- The same path-only check is still at line 105 of current main 513261bb's museum.mjs.

**The original probe reproduces exactly.** I copied it to my own directory with the paths rewritten and ran it. The output matched the finding line for line: ACCEPTED at another Math- commit, ACCEPTED in the query- repository, the card renders "Byte-verified review" with the 1111… or 2222… identity, and the control applied to the proof is REFUSED.

**My own probes refine the finding in three ways. None of them refutes it.**

1. The claim the probe uses, d5-all-height-annulus, cannot be reached through the builder.
   - For that claim build() also uses the review file as replay.source (museum_data.py:414). Moving the review's SOURCES pin therefore moves replay.source too, and museum.mjs:98 refuses the manifest: "Replay command lacks a matching pinned checkout/source".
   - The same protection covers pr22 (d5-height-window) and pr16 (d5-fixed-transverse).
   - So the original frontend demonstration uses a hand-edited museum.json that build() cannot produce. museum_check.py's check_export, which compares museum.json byte for byte with build() output, would reject it.

2. The full path through the builder does work for the other non-pointer reviews.
   - The path is: move the SOURCES pin, read_source accepts the alternate bytes from a plain fixture folder, project() accepts, and the regenerated manifest passes validateBoundManifest.
   - d5-two-scale: the card renders "ACCEPT-scoped / Source label: ACCEPT / Byte-verified review" with review commit aaaa….
   - d6-p15-full-price: validateBoundManifest accepts the manifest. The card does not render offline only because README.md@d6628da (its replay source) is missing from the fixture, the same reason D2 and D4 fail in the baseline. That is a fixture gap, not a defence.
   - Not probed but confirmed by reading the code: d5-inner-belt-density and cumulative-transfer-correction have the same shape as d5-two-scale (no replay command). sard-g-a1-a6-open is an open claim, so the analogous binding would be to status_source, and it is also path-only.
   - So the realistic route is a refresh of the hand-audited SOURCES table that moves one review pin away from MATH_COMMIT. Nothing in the builder, museum_check.py or the frontend would catch it.

3. The query- leg exists only in the frontend.
   - verify_bytes admits only main or Math-, so build() and museum_check.py refuse a query- pin.
   - Only the browser validator, through validateDescriptor at museum.mjs:35, admits query-.
   - The builder line "ACCEPTED (query- repository)" in the original probe comes from project() alone.

**Why important and not critical.** The class, source_label, ACCEPT wording and STATUS quote all stay bound to the pinned index and STATUS bytes, so no status label can be promoted. The route needs an edit by the author side: either a visible commit-hash change in SOURCES, or a hand-edited museum.json, which museum_check.py catches. But "Byte-verified review" then only proves the bytes match their own digest, not that they are the review the pinned index cites. The proof side shows this binding was intended, and the defect has a realistic path for 5 of the 8 non-pointer reviews.

**What this verification does not establish.** It does not change any claim's status. It does not show that any real alternate version of these review files exists; the local Math- clone is shallow and main has a single blob for the sard review. It confers zero organizational-independence credit (same provider).

verdicts.reasoning:
I reproduced this at cd32303 two ways: by re-running the original p2 probes against the existing fixture, without re-running setup.sh, and with my own independent harness under probes/verify_substitution_1/q1_2/ (b_builder.py, f_frontend.mjs, output.txt). Both import the unmodified cd32303 tools/museum_data.py and docs/site/museum.mjs by path. Network is stubbed to throw. Before any mutation, every input was checked against the pins: PROOF_INDEX (the literal embedded in the cd32303 test), STATUS.md, and the pr28 REVIEW.md bytes all match the builder and manifest pins.

Code facts, checked line by line:
- museum.mjs:75 binds a reviewed claim's proof to index_source.repository and commit.
- museum.mjs:86 checks a non-pointer review only with sourceContainsPath(quote, review), which is a path or URL substring test.
- validateDescriptor (line 35) and core.mjs verifiedBytes accept main, Math- and query-.
- In the builder, museum_data.py:405-406 calls descriptor(review_path), which copies whatever SOURCES pin exists for that path. project() never compares it with INDEX.
- At cd32303 every Math- SOURCES pin is at d6628da (verified true), so the shipped museum.json is consistent. Nothing enforces that.

Frontend results. The review on d5-all-height-annulus was replaced by a synthetic alternate (R7 verdict flipped ACCEPT to AMEND) at Math-@1111..., main@2222... and query-@3333.... validateBoundManifest accepts all three. startMuseum renders 'ACCEPT-scoped', 'Source label: ACCEPT' and 'Byte-verified review', with the substituted repository and commit in the review identity block and the review link. The control, the same commit change applied to the proof, is refused: 'Claim proof is not bound by its own pinned source quote'. This confirms the binding was intended and is missing only on the review side.

Extension: the same gap affects the open sard-g-a1-a6-open row. Its review, pinned at main@71400b94, is bound to the STATUS row by path only. A Math-@5555... descriptor carrying unrelated bytes is accepted and shown as 'Byte-verified review'. I also confirmed the check is still path-only on current main 513261bb (docs/site/museum.mjs:105). At cd32303 the frontend tests use review:null or pointer reviews only, so no negative control covers non-pointer review binding.

Correction to the finding's builder half. project() alone does accept the query- variant. The full build()/read_source path calls verify_bytes, which allows only main and Math-, so the builder refuses query- ('invalid source identity'). It still accepts any other Math- commit, and the main repository at any commit. The frontend accepts all three. The core claim is unaffected; only the builder's query- line is overstated.

In scope: museum.mjs, museum_data.py and museum.json are named in the offer. The defect is about immutable source identities, and about which snapshot a cited review belongs to.

Severity: important, not critical.
- The card's ACCEPT class and label still come from the bound index bullet. The alternate review's text is not shown inline; only its link and identity are displayed.
- The bad input needs a change to the hard-coded SOURCES pin in reviewed builder code, for example re-pinning a review to a newer commit, or a same-origin museum.json edit that check_export would catch.
- The path is realistic and nothing would catch it. 'Byte-verified' then proves only that the bytes match their own digest, not that they are the review the pinned index cites.
- The alternate bytes are synthetic. The local Math- clone holds no differing real version of these review files: the blobs at 10e1f191 equal the pins. The finding discloses this.

This review establishes no proof, review or acceptance status for any claim. It is a same-provider review with zero independence credit.

description: The frontend accepts a review pointer when the quote includes its review_url as a raw substring. Any URL that is a prefix of a linked URL also passes the issue-URL regex: main/issues/6 for a bullet linking #65, main/issues/7 for #76, or a truncated comment id. Those pointers are accepted and rendered as 'Review pointer in the verified index' with the 'pinned source binds this review pointer' notice. The builder's check is delimited, so only the browser guard has this gap. A related inconsistency: validateDescriptor enforces the URL shape and review_notice only for pointer_only===true, while validateBoundManifest and renderClaim treat any truthy value as a pointer. verdicts.reasoning:
BYTES. The extracted museum.mjs, core.mjs, museum.json and tools/museum_data.py match the cd32303 git objects (sha256 prefixes 02e9a1f2, 6bbf7fa2, 693a0290, 44b622b9). I checked the PROOF_INDEX.md fixture (f9c4db77…) and STATUS.md (9c3e2114…) against the museum.json pins inside the probe before using them. The cited lines are correct. museum.mjs:85 is `pointerText.includes(claim.review.review_url)`. Line 40 applies the issue-URL regex and the review_notice requirement only when `pointer_only===true`. Lines 82 and 151-154 branch on truthiness. The builder's delimited check is at museum_data.py:403, with the raise on 404.

REPRODUCTION. I re-ran the original probe read-only, without setup.sh, and it gave the observed output exactly. I then wrote an independent harness that does not use common.mjs (probes/verify_substitution_0/q1_3/v_pointer.mjs). The shipped museum.json is ACCEPTED. A non-prefix control, main/issues/99 on D3, is REFUSED, so the guard does check something. Every prefix substitution is ACCEPTED by validateBoundManifest:
- D3 → issues/6
- D3 → a truncated comment id
- D2 → issues/6
- D4 → issues/7
- P15 → issues/6
- AMEND D1 → issues/6

Rendered through startMuseum, the D3 (ACCEPT-scoped) and D1 (AMEND/open) cards show 'Review pointer in the verified index', 'Open review ↗' → https://github.com/d6g8k5htny-coder/main/issues/6, and 'The pinned source binds this review pointer…'. The pinned quote does not link issue #6.

The pointer_only variant also reproduces:
- validateDescriptor throws for pointer_only:true with review_url "", but passes for pointer_only:1 and for "yes".
- The d5-two-scale manifest with pointer_only:1 is ACCEPTED. Its card swaps 'Byte-verified review' (link to TWO_SCALE_REVIEW.md) for 'Review pointer in the verified index' (link to PROOF_INDEX.md) and shows no notice.

The proposed fix works. On a patched copy using `'](' + url + ')'` and `pointer_only===true`, the shipped manifest is still ACCEPTED, and every prefix case and every pointer_only:1 case is REFUSED.

SCOPE. In scope. The defect is in museum.mjs and museum.json, and it is the "mutable review-comment pointers versus immutable pointer-source identities" item of the offer.

SEVERITY: important. The realistic path is stronger than the finding says.
- For reviewed bullets (D2, D3, D4, P15), a hand-edited museum.json is caught in CI by museum_check.py's check_export, so there the browser guard is only defence in depth.
- For the AMEND D1 row, the builder runs no binding check at all: museum_data.py:437-449 never tests review_target against the STATUS row. v_builder.py loads a copy of the builder with the D1 constant changed to main/issues/6. The builder accepts it, and so does the cd32303 browser guard. museum_check.py runs exactly that chain: build, check_export, then the actual-museum frontend test. So a truncated D1 URL lands green.
- With main/issues/9999 instead, the builder still accepts and only the browser guard refuses. The browser substring test is therefore the sole CI guard on the D1 pointer, and a prefix gets past it.

It is not critical. The class/label and the quote, which displays the true review links, stay source-bound. The pointer is labelled not byte-frozen. No status is promoted. The pointer_only:1 sub-issue can only come from a hand-edited museum.json, because the builder always emits a boolean true and check_export catches anything else. Its effect is a downgrade with a missing notice, so on its own it is minor.

CAVEATS (none refute the finding):
1. The proposed delimited fix still cannot tell which link in a quote is the review. Other links in the same quote are accepted before and after the fix: D3 comment 5841779222, D2 comment 5841270276, and D1 task issue #63. All of them are links the source itself attaches to that claim.
2. The builder line is 403; the finding's 404 is the raise line.
3. Context only: on current main 513261bb, D1 must be a byte-bound record (museum.mjs:95). The substring test is still at museum.mjs:104 for D2, D3, D4 and P15, behind the builder's delimited check.

This verification does not establish anything about any claim's mathematical status. It earns zero independence credit, since the reviewer works on the same provider account as the author lane.

I edited the D1 URL in an in-memory copy of the builder in three ways: issues/6, a one-digit-truncated comment id (584183074), and the erratum comment. For the ACCEPT cards, getting a bad pointer displayed needs a museum.json that bypasses check_export. In other words, the browser guard is defense-in-depth there.

But the guard does certify a link to an unrelated issue or comment as bound by the source, and there is a realistic CI-passing path on the D1 card. The finding is in scope: museum.mjs, under the offer's item "mutable review-comment pointers versus immutable pointer-source identities". verdicts.reasoning:
I reproduced the central claim against the cd32303 bytes. I copied the probe into probes/verify_substitution_0/ and repointed HERE there, so it does not overwrite the original fixture. setup.sh re-verified the fixture: PROOF_INDEX sha256 f9c4db77, plus 21 Math- sources checked against their pinned identities. No network was used: fetch is stubbed, and every served byte matches its pinned digest. The p4 output matched the reported output line for line.

The code agrees with the probe:
- museum.mjs:100 only calls validateDescriptor on exhibits ec014, remote, annulus and p15.
- museum.mjs:101 applies sameIdentity to exhibits.lifetime alone.
- museum.mjs:197-199 checks exhibit_quotes[kind] against that exhibit's own fetched bytes.
- geometry.mjs:386-391 binds the repository to Math- and the path to SOURCE_PATHS[kind]. It checks that commit and sha256 are well-formed but does not tie them to any value.

So an exhibit at the same path but at another commit, with matching digests and a matching excerpt, passes. It renders under object-label 'D5 all-height fixed annulus', reached from the D5 ACCEPT card's 'Open source illustration' link, and its 'Exact source excerpt' shows the widened scope. The identical change on lifetime is refused. docs/site/README.md at cd32303 says 'The museum binds Math sources to d6628da...', and the browser-side guard does not enforce that for these exhibits. The defect is still present on main 513261bb (museum.mjs:120-121, unchanged).

Separate checks I added:
1. The builder ties each exhibit to its claim structurally. SOURCES holds one identity per path, and v1_ci_gate.py shows remote, annulus, p15 and lifetime identical to claims 2, 3, 10 and 0 on all 8 identity fields. museum_check.py runs on every PR and push in public-shop.yml, and its check_export compares bytes. It refuses the substituted manifest ('generated museum export differs'). So the current CI blocks this exact substitution.

Why I still rate it important rather than minor:
- Pages is 'Deploy from a branch -> main -> /docs', so whatever is on main is served whatever CI says. I did not verify whether branch protection requires the check.
- A plausible future builder change could give exhibits their own identities, for example pointing an illustration at newer Math- text. CI would then go green and the browser validator, the documented display-time guard, would stay silent.
- tests/test_museum_frontend.mjs has no negative control for this. Its fixture uses the same descriptor for every exhibit.

Why not critical: the exhibit card shows the substituted commit (4444...), is classed 'illustration', and carries 'It is not a proof and does not change status'. It shows no ACCEPT label. The D5 claim card keeps its own d6628da identity and its ACCEPT label.

Corrections to the finding:
- (a) The secondary path-swap sub-claim is accurate only at the validateBoundManifest level. In the render, the end state is always a refusal. With exhibit_quotes.remote unchanged, the quote check refuses first ('Exhibit quote differs from the pinned source'), before any card is appended. Only when the quote is also changed does geometry.mjs refuse, after the card was briefly appended. So 'only geometry.mjs refuses it later' overstates; that sub-case is not a display defect.
- (b) The '3 source view(s) unavailable' state line is unrelated to the exhibit. It comes from README.md@d6628da missing offline, which refuses the D2, D4 and D6 claim cards through their replay sources. The exhibit job itself succeeds.
- (c) The probe's alternative bytes are a synthetic stand-in. That is adequate, because only museum.json digests are checked, and the original probe labels them as synthetic.
- (d) The finding lists the D5 height-window card as linking to view=annulus. That is correct, and in the shipped state that exhibit is the all-height proof, honestly labelled 'D5 all-height fixed annulus'.

This verification does not establish the following:
- Whether branch protection makes public-shop a required check.
- Whether a commit with altered bytes exists in Math-.
- Anything about the mathematical status of any claim. Scientific effect is NONE, and as a same-provider reviewer I earn zero organizational-independence credit.

BYTES. I checked that the extracted museum.mjs (02e9a1f2…), geometry.mjs (29b9cfd9…) and museum.json (693a0290…) are byte-identical to `git show cd32303:<path>`. I rebuilt the fixture in my own directory, <SCRATCH>/museum/probes/verify_substitution_1/q1_4/. Its PROOF_INDEX sha256 is f9c4db77…, which equals index_source. The annulus PROOF.md sha256 is d55e2c03…, which equals the pin. All probes import museum.mjs and geometry.mjs straight from the cd32303 tree, and fetch is stubbed out.

REPRODUCED. The original p4 probe gives the same output as the finding. I extended it in v4b. The same commit-only substitution also works for exhibits.remote, which renders under 'D4 fixed-remote RN', and exhibits.p15, which renders under 'D6 P15 full price'. In both cases the widened excerpt is shown as 'Exact source excerpt'. The code matches the cited lines:
- museum.mjs:100 only calls validateDescriptor.
- museum.mjs:101 applies sameIdentity to lifetime alone.
- museum.mjs:197-199 checks the quote against the exhibit's own bytes.
- geometry.mjs:386-390 binds the repository and path, but the commit and sha256 are checked only with a regex.

The tests have no negative control for this. test_museum_frontend.mjs sets every exhibit to the same `proof` descriptor and asserts only the lifetime binding. The gap is unchanged in current main 513261bb: museum.mjs:120-121 still binds lifetime only. docs/site/README.md says 'The museum binds Math sources to d6628da…', and the browser does not enforce that for these three exhibits.

IN SCOPE. The defect is in docs/site/museum.mjs, which is in the offer, and geometry.mjs, which the pickup added. It is a cross-claim and cross-version substitution at the interface between museum.json and museum.mjs.

QUALIFICATIONS. These do not refute the finding, but they limit how realistic the path is.
(1) The data shipped at cd32303 is correct. exhibits.remote, annulus and p15 have the same identity as claims[2], [3] and [10].proof. That holds by construction: museum_data.build takes every descriptor from SOURCES, a dict keyed by path that holds one identity per path. So the current builder cannot emit a different commit for the same path without restructuring SOURCES.
(2) CI (public-shop.yml) runs tools/museum_check.py, which regenerates museum.json and compares bytes. A hand-edited exhibit commit therefore fails CI (v4a).
(3) museum.json is served from the same origin as museum.mjs, so the browser check is a second line of defence, not a defence against an attacker.
(4) The finding's sub-claim about swapping in another claim's path is accurate but small. validateBoundManifest accepts the swap. geometry.mjs then refuses it, and the final page shows 'Unavailable: Geometry source identity does not match the exhibit'. The wrong card is visible only while geometry.mjs loads, and the excerpt is never shown (v4b).
(5) 'Why it matters' overstates the present exposure. With the shipped bytes and CI, no reader can land on such an excerpt today.

SEVERITY. I keep 'important', not 'critical' or 'minor'. The realistic path is a future builder change, which would pass both CI and the browser, because CI only checks that museum.json equals the builder output and no test binds these exhibits to claims. An example is re-pinning the illustrations to a newer Math- commit while the reviewed claims stay at d6628da. The author's own lifetime rule exists for exactly that case: the builder binds lifetime by construction too, yet the author added a browser sameIdentity check. The three omitted exhibits are more prominent than lifetime: they are linked from ACCEPT-scoped cards, carry claim titles and show an 'Exact source excerpt'. It is not critical, because no bad input reaches the guard at cd32303 and the card shows the real commit plus the illustration disclaimer.

SIDE NOTE, not part of this finding. The D5 height-window card (claims[4], proof rn_thin_tube…/FIXED_ANNULUS_CANDIDATE.md) also links to view=annulus, whose source is the D5 all-height proof. A fix should bind each exhibit by its key (annulus to claims[3], remote to claims[2], p15 to claims[10]), not by the card that links to it.

Scientific effect NONE. This verification grants zero organizational-independence credit, because the reviewer is on the same provider. It does not establish anything about the mathematics, about how the deployed site behaves in a real browser, or whether a real alternate commit of these files exists. The local Math- clone is shallow, so the substituted bytes are synthetic.

Verdict: reproduced, not refuted, in scope, severity important.

How it was run. I copied the original probe into my own directory (verify_substitution_0/q1_5/) so I would not touch the fixture used by the other lens. setup.sh re-derives PROOF_INDEX.md@d6628da from the INDEX_BYTES embedded in cd32303 tests/test_museum_data.py: 12708 bytes, blob e4cb1d94, sha256 f9c4db77, which equals SOURCES["PROOF_INDEX.md"]. All 21 other Math- sources were byte-verified from local git objects. Re-running p5_replay_binding.py and p5_replay_binding.mjs gave output identical to the finding's.

Code reading at cd32303 agrees with the finding:
- The commands are hard-coded in CLAIM_SPECS (tools/museum_data.py:263-341).
- project() at lines 410-418 sets replay_source = "README.md" for status_id D2, D4 and D6 and never compares the command with any text. build() verifies the README bytes but does not use them.
- validateBoundManifest (museum.mjs:96-98) checks the replay's shape, that the source repository and commit equal the proof's, and that checkout equals proof.commit. Nothing ties the command to the claim.
- verifyClaim (museum.mjs:118) only checks that the command equals some trimmed line of the verified replay source.
- In shipped museum.json, D2, D4 and D6 share one identical README descriptor. So for those three claims the check is a test of membership in a set shared by all three claims.
- The only replay negative control is an invented command (test_museum_frontend.mjs:47-49 and 149-150). The test at line 127 is nevertheless titled "...rejects cross-claim source, scope and replay substitutions".

Stronger check through the full CI gate (my own probe):
- e2e_q15.sh copies the cd32303 tree and patches only the copy's builder: README.md is re-pinned to the Math-@10e1f191 stand-in bytes (README@d6628da, blob abe16871, is in no local repository), and CLAIM_SPECS is edited. It then regenerates museum.json and runs the copy's own tools/museum_check.py, which rebuilds, runs check_export and then node --test tests/test_museum_frontend.mjs, including the "actual pinned museum" test.
- The baseline passes (15/15).
- The D2<->D6 swap with D4 given the D0 hard_gate.py passes (15/15).
- Giving all three cards full_price.py passes (15/15).
- The control, D2 given an invented command, fails test 15. So the gate is not vacuous.
- Rendering through startMuseum shows the swapped commands on the wrong cards under the banner "Source projections and displayed source bytes verified".

Why the stand-in README does not weaken the result. A pure permutation among D2, D4 and D6 passes against any README that contains the three original commands. CI at cd32303 requires exactly that, because the actual-museum test needs all 14 cards verified. So a swap of commands that each passed CI for their own card passes again, for any README. Only the hard_gate.py substitution depends on unverified d6628da README content. That line is present at the earlier 10e1f191, and the d6628da README is larger (6023 bytes against 5638).

Specific to README-sourced claims. For D5 the replay source is each claim's own review. Each review holds its own command (control: True), and none holds another D5 claim's command (four cross-checks: False). Their binding is therefore effective in CI, which confirms the defect is confined to the shared-README claims.

One part of the finding overstates its realistic path: the P15 counterexample sub-case.
- Giving the engineering-only P15 counterexample a command through CLAIM_SPECS makes the builder fail with KeyError, because the review path is an https URL with no SOURCES entry.
- That case is reachable only by editing museum.json directly. CI's check_export would reject that edit; the browser does not run check_export.
- So it shows a gap in the frontend guard (validateBoundManifest accepts it, and the card shows the full_price.py replay while staying class engineering-only), not a path through CI.
The core D2/D4/D6 path does go through CI: a copy-paste error in the hand-maintained CLAIM_SPECS passes every check.

Severity. Not critical:
- Every card keeps "Finite algebra or implementation replay only; it is not theorem acceptance".

- The hard-coded engineering strip says replay output does not change status.
- No proof, review or acceptance is shown that the source does not support.
Not minor: it is a real binding defect on a realistic path, and it is hidden by a test whose title claims to cover cross-claim replay substitution.

I reproduced this against the cd32303 bytes. I copied the author probe into probes/verify_substitution_1/q1_5/, pointed its paths there, and re-ran setup.sh, p5_replay_binding.py and p5_replay_binding.mjs. The output matched the reported output line for line. I also wrote two probes of my own, v5a_builder.py and v5b_frontend.mjs. All output is in q1_5/ALL_OUTPUT.txt.

What is true at cd32303:
(1) The builder never compares a command with any source. museum_data.py:263-341 hard-codes the commands, and at 410-418 the command is copied into the replay with replay_source = README.md for D2, D4 and D6. Even an invented command ('python invented-solver.py') is accepted (v5a #1). The same builder does refuse a misdirected review pointer (v5a #3) and checks proof paths against the bullet. So the hard-coded specs are not trusted for proof and review, but they are trusted for the replay.
(2) museum.mjs:95-98 checks only the replay's shape, its repository and commit against the proof, and its checkout. A D2<->D6 swap, and the P15 counterexample given D6's replay, are both ACCEPTED (A2, A4). A D2<->D6 proof swap is REFUSED (A5).
(3) museum.mjs:118 only tests that the command is one of the trimmed lines of replay.source. D2, D4 and D6 share one identical replay.source descriptor (C1: sha256 89d4c618..., 6023 bytes). So any permutation of their three commands gives the same membership result as the shipped commands. The shipped CI path (museum_check.py -> test_museum_frontend 'actual pinned museum renders all cards') needs every shipped command to pass against the real README@d6628da, so on the real bytes the D2<->D6 swap must pass as well. This follows from the code and does not depend on the README's content.
(4) End to end through startMuseum, using a labelled stand-in: the real README@10e1f191 bytes served at the d6628da URL under their own sha256. The baseline renders all 14 cards as verified. The swapped manifest (D2 shows full_price.py, D6 shows the three_fronts unittest, D4 shows hard_gate.py) also renders all 14 cards: 'displayed source bytes verified', nothing refused. As a control, an invented D4 command is refused.
(5) Only the two replay commands differ between a swapped CLAIM_SPECS and the shipped export (v5a #5). check_export therefore follows the builder, so a CLAIM_SPECS edit passes every CI gate.
(6) The cd32303 test is named 'rejects cross-claim source, scope and replay substitutions', but its replay case only tries an invented command. That shows replay substitution was meant to be inside the cross-claim guard, so this is in scope.
The same replay logic is still in current main 513261bb: museum.mjs:115-118 and 137-140.

Corrections to the finding text. None of them changes the verdict.
(a) 'The builder and validateBoundManifest accept all of these' overstates the P15 sub-case. The builder cannot give the P15 counterexample a command at all: its status_id is None, so replay_source falls back to its review path, an issue URL that is not in SOURCES. The result is KeyError (v5a #4). That sub-case is reachable only through a hand-edited museum.json, which validateBoundManifest and verifyClaim accept but CI's check_export would reject.
(b) The verifyClaim lines in the author probe use a descriptor at commit 10e1f191, not the pin. Whether hard_gate.py is a line of README@d6628da cannot be checked offline: blob abe16871 is in no local clone. It is a line at 10e1f191, so the D4/hard_gate sub-case is plausible but not proven at the pin. The D2<->D6 swap needs no README bytes (point 3).

Severity: important, not critical. The class, the source label and the STATUS quote stay correctly bound. The replay column carries 'Finite algebra or implementation replay only; it is not theorem acceptance.' So no acceptance or status is misrepresented. It is still a real interface defect with a realistic path: a hand-edit or copy error in the hard-coded commands, for example when the pin moves, passes the builder, check_export and the actual-museum frontend test. The card would then present another package's run as this claim's replay. A claim-specific binding is easy to get, because each command's package directory matches its proof's directory. This review earns zero organizational-independence credit and has no scientific effect.

No guard or test in the museum CI refuses this, and the generator-side test that is supposed to keep review custody honest (test_review_pointers_do_not_claim_comment_byte_custody) checks only the pointer_only key. The guards whose job is to check generator output independently (validateBoundManifest, and the museum_check integration test) pass that input. This is the asymmetry described above: the same substitution made in the identity is refused.

description: The browser guard accepts a pointer review_url if it is a substring of the pinned quote. Because issue numbers and comment ids are digit strings, any truncation is a different, regex-valid GitHub pointer. Examples: .../issues/6 is a prefix of .../issues/67#issuecomment-..., .../issues/7 is a prefix of .../issues/76#..., and #issuecomment-584 or #issuecomment-58412 are prefixes of real comment ids. On the generator side, project() accepts any markdown link target in a reviewed bullet as the review: D2 can take '[main #67](.../issues/67)', which the bullet says 'remains open for other bundled fronts'. For the three AMEND rows the generator checks nothing, so an edited D1 target of .../issues/6 regenerates and passes the full museum CI. In every case the card shows 'Review pointer in the verified index' with the substituted link, and the details show the genuine pointer-source digest, so the pinned identity appears to vouch for a pointer that the pinned bytes do not contain. The only frontend negative control ('review comment pointers cannot masquerade...') uses a URL absent from the quote, so it cannot detect a prefix.
why: For mutable pointers, the pinned pointer source is the only immutable anchor. Its binding guarantee ('Review pointer is not bound by its pinned source quote') is weaker than its error message: a displayed review link can lead to a different issue or comment than the one the pinned index or STATUS bytes cite, while the card shows the pinned digest as its authority. Fix: parse markdown link targets from the quoted line and require review_url to equal one of them exactly, and, in project(), apply the same exact check to the AMEND-row targets.

title: A 'Byte-verified review' is bound by path suffix only: repository and commit are never tied to the pinned pointer source, and a mutable blob/main link satisfies the binding

description: In the pinned index, a relative review link like '](reviews/pr28.../REVIEW.md)' identifies an immutable object only together with the index's own identity, Math-@d6628da. The guard never enforces that. (a) The d5-pin AMEND card's pointer descriptor is PROOF_INDEX@d6628da. With pointer_only removed, the STATUS row's mutable link 'https://github.com/d6g8k5htny-coder/Math-/blob/main/PROOF_INDEX.md)' matches the '/PROOF_INDEX.md)' clause, so a branch-relative URL is accepted as binding a pinned identity, and the card flips from 'Review pointer' to 'Byte-verified review'. The same removal is refused on the other five pointer cards (control). (b) The same review path at another commit or repository (Math-@bebb77ae, or query-@ffff...) passes validation, and passes fetch-verification wherever bytes at that identity hash to the descriptor's own sha256. (c) A file named just REVIEW.md in any allowed repository, at any commit, is 'contained' in every quote that links some .../REVIEW.md. The probe serves forged bytes with a self-consistent digest at that identity, standing in for a file that someone with write access could publish. (d) Overlaps the substitution lens: a claim's own proof can fill its review slot, so D2's comment pointer becomes a 'Byte-verified review' of LIFETIME_REMAINDER.md. Today's committed data is consistent: every review is at d6628da or 71400b94. The defect is in the guard.
why: 'Byte-verified review' is supposed to mean 'the review the pinned source points at, frozen'. The guard proves only 'some bytes whose path ends like a link in the quote'. A branch-relative (mutable) link is accepted as the binding, and nothing ties the review's commit to the snapshot that cites it. Fix: resolve relative links against the quoting source's repository and commit, require review.repository and review.commit to equal them (as is already done for proof), drop the '/${path})' suffix clause, and refuse non-pointer reviews whose identity equals a pointer source.

description: On the actual cd32303 manifest, six cards rest their review on a mutable GitHub pointer. Three are ACCEPT-scoped (D2, D3, D4), one is engineering-only (P15, a whole open issue thread rather than a comment), and two are AMEND (D1 and d5-pin). On every one the green strip reads 'Source byte count and SHA-256 verified. Review wording is quoted at its declared scope.' But the only quotes on those cards are the PROOF_INDEX bullet or STATUS row, plus a STATUS cell. Those are the index author's 'review descriptions', which the pinned index itself dates ('checked on 2026-09-26'). The museum drops that date. The 'review' fetch step for a pointer card verifies the pointer source's bytes again, not the review. I simulated an edit that withdraws the ACCEPT, served at every review URL: the viewer makes 0 requests to github.com, and the rendered cards and page state are byte-identical. The per-card notice ('not byte-frozen') partly mitigates this. But the strip, the page-level 'displayed source bytes verified' and the absence of the dated qualifier together present an undated review description as quoted review wording, which nothing would update if a review comment were edited or deleted.
why: This answers the lens question 'can an edited comment silently change what is shown without any check failing?' The page never shows the comment, so the page does not change. What changes is the review behind three ACCEPT-scoped cards, while those cards keep asserting that review wording is quoted and verified. Fix: on pointer cards, replace the strip with something like 'Review is a mutable GitHub comment; only the pinned index/STATUS pointer is byte-verified', and show the index's own date ('review descriptions checked on 2026-09-26'). If custody is wanted, land the comment bodies as byte-pinned files and point at those.

description:
read_source() is the only way museum_data.build() and museum_check.py get bytes. It runs `git show <commit>:<path>` and, if that fails for any reason (the path is absent at that commit, the commit is unknown, a shallow checkout, or not a repository at all), it reads the file from the root's working tree. Only size, git blob id and sha256 are then checked. Nothing checks that <path> is in the tree of <commit>, which is exactly what 'packet membership at the declared snapshot' means.

I moved the main pin to bd9fc9d6, a real main commit (the parent of the packet's landing commit d10c2fb). Its STATUS.md, SARD review and notebook are byte-identical to the pins, but it has no incoming/ directory. With only that pin changed, the PR's generator emits museum.json with the packet 'at' bd9fc9d6, and the PR's CI gate tools/museum_check.py passes 15 of 15 node tests and exits 0. That includes the test 'actual pinned museum renders all cards', which renders the packet card with Commit bd9fc9d6.... The unit test test_landed_packet_can_be_read_from_pinned_sparse_checkout also passes.

Under strict raw-at-commit semantics the same manifest renders 'Packet source Unavailable: Source unavailable (404)'. So the deployed page fails closed, but the guard that claims to bind membership to the snapshot passes on a non-member.

The Git-versus-plain-file choice also depends on the environment. It depends only on whether git show succeeds in whatever repository git discovers from cwd. With a discoverable repository that holds 71400b94 (GIT_DIR, or a TMPDIR inside a full clone), the PR's own control test_plain_fixture_directory_does_not_bypass_byte_verification fails with 'ValueError not raised'. No test checks that a commit lacking the path is refused.
why: The docs say main 'source/packet membership' is bound to 71400b94, and museum_check.py is the gate meant to enforce that. In fact the gate checks bytes against whatever the checkout's working tree (HEAD) holds, so membership is computed from a moving ref rather than the declared commit. A snapshot refresh that pins a packet to a commit where it does not exist goes green in CI and only appears after deploy, as a refusal card. The live page fails closed, so no status is misrepresented, but the guard passes on bad input. The fix is to refuse when a git root lacks <commit>:<path>, keeping plain-fixture reads to an explicit fixture mode, and to add a negative control for a path absent at a present commit.

Its only object source is a read-only alternates file pointing at /home/user/main/.git/objects, and GIT_DIR is not set. This is closer to the CI checkout than the original probe's GIT_DIR approach: public-shop.yml uses actions/checkout with fetch-depth: 0, so the full history is present and git is discovered from the repo.

- V1 (read_source): the pinned RESULT.md is accepted at three commits.
  - 71400b94: the declared pin; the path is a member (control).
  - bd9fc9d6: a real main commit and the parent of d10c2fb, the commit that landed the packet. `git ls-tree` shows 0 `incoming/` entries there and 3 at 71400b94.
  - f*40: a commit that does not exist.
  - Control (d): delete the working-tree file and the bd9fc9d6 read is REFUSED with FileNotFoundError, while 71400b94 is still accepted from objects. This shows the bytes accepted at bd9fc9d6 came from the working tree.
- V2b (CI gate): I made a complete refresh to bd9fc9d6, replacing the pin in tools/museum_data.py, the test literal, README and IMPLEMENTATION, then regenerated museum.json. The whole museum step of public-shop.yml went green:
  - `unittest` test_museum_data: 12 tests, OK
  - museum_check.py: 15/15, exit 0
  - test_museum_geometry: 8/8
  - Yet all three packet paths are NOT-MEMBER at bd9fc9d6. STATUS.md, the SARD review and the notebook are members, with identical blob ids.
- V3 (rendering): I ran cd32303 museum.mjs on that manifest.
  - Harness mode, which serves the bytes museum_check.py feeds through MUSEUM_FIXTURE, renders the packet card with "Commit bd9fc9d6...".
  - Strict raw-at-commit mode renders "Packet source Unavailable: Source unavailable (404). No result inferred."

CORRECTION. The finding says that with "only that pin changed" the gate passes. That is true of tools/museum_check.py alone (15/15, exit 0, reproduced in V2). The full CI step, however, runs the unittest discover first. Its test_packet_selection_excludes_unknown_fork_packet hardcodes 71400b94 (tests/test_museum_data.py:91) and fails when only museum_data.py changes. That literal mirrors the pin and detects a change; it does not check membership. Any refresh updates it together with the pin, and then CI is green. So "goes green in CI" holds for a realistic, complete refresh, and the finding should say that the test literal must also be updated.

SCOPE AND LIMITS.
- Math- is not affected in CI. CI runs museum_check.py without --math-root, so Math- sources come from urlopen on the commit-pinned raw URL, which enforces membership. My probes used --math-root only because probes have no network access, and the Math- pins were left untouched. The defect applies to main pins, which is where the packet is.
- The fallback runs only when `git show` fails. A path that is present at the commit with different bytes is still refused. The hole is limited to a path that is absent at the commit, or a commit that is unknown.
- From reading the code (not executed): test_museum_frontend.mjs has a strict `git show` path, used when MUSEUM_MATH_ROOT is set and MUSEUM_FIXTURE is not, which would catch this. museum_check.py always sets MUSEUM_FIXTURE, so CI never exercises that path. I could not run the strict mode because Math- d6628da is not available locally.
- The sub-claim that the source choice depends on the environment also reproduces without GIT_DIR. With TMPDIR inside a discovered repo that holds 71400b94, test_plain_fixture_directory_does_not_bypass_byte_verification fails ("ValueError not raised"); with TMPDIR unset it passes. That failure is a false red, not a false green, and default GitHub Actions passes, so this part is minor.
- The original probe's p1_fallback_unit.py re-ran with output identical to what the finding reports.

SEVERITY: important, not critical. The deployed page fails closed and shows a refusal card. The packet is engineering-only with scientific_effect NONE, and no proof, review, acceptance or status is misrepresented. It is still a real interface defect on a realistic path:
- docs/site/README.md:48 says the museum binds "main source/packet membership" to 71400b94, and IMPLEMENTATION W9 says it projects "only the single packet present at the main snapshot".
- The gate does not enforce either statement, and no test refuses a pin whose commit lacks the path.
- The realistic error is pinning a refresh to the latest main from before a packet lands. bd9fc9d6 is exactly that commit.
- The review offer names "packet membership at the declared snapshot" explicitly.

With that change, the generator, museum_check (exit 0, 15 of 15 node tests) and a strict raw-at-commit render all report 'displayed source bytes verified' while showing one packet. why: The README says the list shows the submissions present in the pinned default-branch snapshot, a completeness claim that no guard enforces. Omission only hides a packet that carries no status effect, so this is minor. But the 'landed packet index' is not derived from the snapshot it names, and a refresh can silently drop members. The fix is to compare packet_descriptors() with `git ls-tree -d <commit> incoming/` in museum_check, and to compute the summary line.

(1) MAIN_COMMIT (tools/museum_data.py:20) is never read: an AST scan finds zero load-uses. The main pin is spelled out separately in each of the six main SOURCES entries.
(2) packet_descriptors() (lines 454-460) takes no arguments and returns a one-element list literal. Its docstring says "Only the packet already present on the pinned main tree is selected."
(3) Line 553's success line is a constant string, not computed. Its "11 bullets / 3 AMEND rows" counts are enforced by raises in project(); its "1 landed packet" is not.
(4) None of the seven in-scope files (museum_data.py, museum_check.py, museum.mjs, geometry.mjs and the three tests) enumerates incoming/: no ls-tree, iterdir, listdir, glob, walk or readdir.
(5) museum.mjs:102 accepts 0 or 1 packets. Line 107 checks only that each listed packet's commit equals status_source.commit, which is soundness, not completeness. Line 191 prints "No packet appears in this pinned projection."
(6) At 71400b94 the list is exactly right: ls-tree shows one packet, museum.json lists one, and the regeneration is byte-identical.
(7) a12c178c is the real main merge of #150, and #151's merge d77a85a7 is its ancestor. Its incoming/ holds two packets. All six pinned main sources have the same blob ids there, so a refresh to it regenerates cleanly.

CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING'S WORDING:
(a) "Every guard green" holds only for a complete refresh. The finding's own simulation changed museum_data.py alone and ran only museum_check. Under that exact change the first command of the CI step fails: tests/test_museum_data.py:91 hard-codes the commit (AssertionError 'a12c178c...' != '71400b94...'), shown in V1(B). That test pins a commit, not membership, and a reviewed refresh updates it as a matter of course. After that update all guards are green, so the conclusion stands. Note also that test line 87 asserts exactly one id, which is a second hard-coded expectation.
(b) docs/site/README.md:56 explicitly says "only the one package in the pinned main snapshot", so the count is documented. The real gap is that README.md:96's completeness wording ("shows submissions present in its pinned default-branch snapshot") is not derived from or checked against the declared commit.

Scope: "packet membership at the declared snapshot" is named in the offer (comment 5848315997), so this is in scope. It affects robustness only and has no effect on scientific status. Fix: call cancel() (or response.body?.cancel()) before the early return. No test covers it.

That branch binds the pointer only by pointerText.includes(review_url), so review_url '' is accepted (String.prototype.includes('') === true), as is any substring of the quote, such as 'D2'. Effects:
- The card shows 'Review pointer in the verified index'.
- 'Open review' points at PROOF_INDEX.md itself, or at a relative link like 'D2'.
- The 'linked review is not byte-frozen' notice is dropped.
- A byte-frozen review file (d5-two-scale, or the STATUS-pinned sard-g review) can be replaced by a pseudo-pointer to the Math- index, and the banner still says verified.

why: The interface's own distinction between a mutable review-comment pointer and an immutable source identity, which is part of the offered scope, can be bypassed with an unexpected type. The disclosure that the linked review is not byte-frozen is then removed. Fix: require typeof pointer_only === 'boolean' (or reject any value other than true/absent) everywhere, branch on === true in validateBoundManifest and renderClaim, and require review_url non-empty and equal to one exact link target of the quote.
